name: Midline Cervical Cleft

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Clinical Diagnostic Criteria for Midline Cervical Cleft

criteria.description: Presence of a midline vertical skin defect on the anterior neck
Superior skin tag or nipple-like projection at the upper end of the cleft
Subcutaneous fibrous cord or band extending inferiorly from the cleft
No associated thyroid gland malformations on imaging

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of the midline skin cleft with superior skin tag and subcutaneous fibrous tract
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis is primarily clinical; imaging may be used to exclude other anomalies.

searchTerms: vertical skin split on front of neck
skin groove running down neck center

pathognomonic.symptomName: Superior skin tag or nipple-like projection on anterior neck
searchTerms: small skin tag or nipple-like bump on neck

pathognomonic.symptomName: Subcutaneous fibrous cord extending inferiorly from cleft
searchTerms: fibrous band under skin extending downward

common.symptomName: Restricted neck extension due to fibrous band
searchTerms: limited neck movement from fibrous band
neck stiffness due to skin band
mild extra skin fold on side of neck

occasional.symptomName: Scar contracture leading to neck flexion deformity
Mild dysphagia due to neck contracture
searchTerms: mild swallowing problems due to neck contracture

occasional.symptomName: Superficial ulceration or irritation of cleft skin
searchTerms: skin sores or irritation on neck cleft
occasional fluid or pus from neck sinus

rare.symptomName: Respiratory distress due to neck contracture
searchTerms: trouble breathing due to neck contracture
respiratory problems caused by neck stiffness

imaging: Ultrasound to exclude thyroid gland abnormalities
MRI or CT to assess extent of fibrous tract and exclude deep neck anomalies
genetic: No specific genetic mutation identified; sporadic congenital malformation
other: Clinical examination revealing characteristic midline cervical cleft with superior skin tag and inferior fibrous band

distinguishingFeatures: Lateral neck location versus midline in cervical cleft
Presence of cystic mass rather than skin cleft
No superior skin tag or fibrous cord
Midline neck cyst but typically located higher near hyoid bone
No skin cleft or fibrous band
Moves with swallowing or tongue protrusion

redFlags: Rapidly increasing neck swelling or mass
Signs of infection such as fever or purulent discharge
references: Berkowitz RG, et al. Midline cervical cleft: clinical features and surgical management. Int J Pediatr Otorhinolaryngol. 2003.
Sadler TW. Langman's Medical Embryology. 14th Edition. 2019.
